q: Which departments is the model losing to the naive baseline, and why might that be?

output.note: volume_units is total units sold over the 263-day backtest window

answer:
Five of the seven departments have negative FVA — the model is losing to seasonal-naive in HOUSEHOLD_1 (-9.4 pp), HOUSEHOLD_2 (-7.6 pp), FOODS_1 (-7.3 pp), FOODS_3 (-7.0 pp) and FOODS_2 (-0.9 pp). Only HOBBIES_2 (+10.6 pp) and HOBBIES_1 (+2.8 pp) add value; pooled FVA is -5.7 pp (model 79.5% vs naive 85.2%).

Why, from the evidence available:
1) The naive baseline is hardest to beat exactly where the model loses. The three biggest losses sit on the three most stable series: HOUSEHOLD_1 naive accuracy 87.8%, FOODS_3 87.1%, HOUSEHOLD_2 86.6%. Where the baseline is weak — HOBBIES_2 naive 54.9% — the model wins by a wide margin. Stable weekly demand means 'repeat last week's same weekday' is already near-optimal.
2) The model's daily output looks close to flat, so it gives up the day-of-week/holiday signal the naive gets for free. In FOODS_3's worst days the model prints 2497.5 units on 2013-08-25, 2013-09-01, 2013-09-08 and 2013-09-29 while actuals ranged 3751–4042 and naive erred by only 176–642 units; HOUSEHOLD_1 shows the same repeated 610.7 value on 2013-06-02, 2013-06-09 and 2013-07-21.
3) Closure/holiday days hurt it hardest: on 2013-12-25 actuals were 0 but the model predicted 2431.5 units in FOODS_3 and 646.9 in HOUSEHOLD_1 — larger misses than the naive's 1755.0 and 392.0.

Bias is not the main culprit: signed bias is small in the losing departments (FOODS_3 -0.7%, HOUSEHOLD_2 +3.0%, FOODS_1 -3.9%, HOUSEHOLD_1 +4.1%, FOODS_2 -4.2%), so the problem is shape/timing, not level. Recent weeks confirm the gap persists: week of 2014-01-20 model 68.8% vs naive 89.9%.

answer:
No — the premise doesn't hold. Prophet's WAPE is measured on daily units and Elastic Net's on monthly aggregates; monthly aggregation cancels day-to-day noise, so the two numbers are not comparable head-to-head and the gap is not a like-for-like quality difference. The backtest study reports both side by side with exactly that caveat.

What the numbers actually are (Prophet daily WAPE vs Elastic Net monthly WAPE): FOODS_3 19.81% vs 4.86%; HOUSEHOLD_1 21.56% vs 3.26%; HOBBIES_1 18.57% vs 4.32%; FOODS_2 20.55% vs 5.31%; FOODS_1 24.99% vs 6.96%; HOUSEHOLD_2 20.94% vs 8.99%; HOBBIES_2 34.32% vs 58.96%.

Two further points against a blanket switch: (1) even on its own easier monthly basis, Elastic Net is worse than Prophet's daily figure in HOBBIES_2 (58.96% vs 34.32%), the thinnest department at 23.6 mean daily units — so the ranking isn't even uniform; (2) the two models answer different questions. Daily replenishment needs a daily forecast; a monthly-aggregate model can't be dropped into that role. Choose by planning horizon, not by comparing these two WAPEs. A genuine comparison would need both models scored on the same granularity, which this backtest does not provide.
